items.title: Anatomising Irish rebellion: the Cromwellian delinquency commissions, the books of discrimination and the 1641 depositions
items.note: Explains the 1653–4 'delinquency depositions' within the collection, which were gathered to assign guilt for the land settlement and must be weighed differently from 1641–2 testimony.

items.title: Portadown, 1641: Memory and the 1641 Depositions
items.note: Separates eyewitness, hearsay and later testimony on the Portadown drownings, showing how one atrocity was reported in divergent versions and numbers.

items.title: Religion, ethnicity and "conversion" in the 1641 Irish Rebellion
items.note: Uses the depositions to examine forced and voluntary conversion during the rising, which bears on who was counted as a Protestant victim.

items.title: Children's Experiences of Violence during the Irish Rebellion of 1641
items.note: Studies how deponents recorded violence against and witnessed by children, a category often folded into aggregate claims of the dead.

items.title: Publication of Volume VI of the 1641 Depositions series (King's and Queen's Counties)
items.who: Irish Manuscripts Commission (A. Clarke et al.)
items.note: Continues the twelve-volume print edition of the depositions; the IMC's announcements suggest some volumes, such as Wexford, appeared as late as 2024.

items.title: Religion, civility and the 'British' of Ireland in the 1641 Irish rebellion
items.note: Analyses a neglected 1643 treatise by Henry Jones and fellow deposition commissioners, the men who shaped how the testimony was collected and framed.

items.title: Crowds and political violence in early modern Ireland: Galway and the 1641 depositions
items.note: Reconstructs crowd violence in Galway from the depositions, showing patterns of attack, restraint and plunder outside Ulster.

items.title: 1641 Depositions [review of the digital edition]
items.note: Reviews the Trinity College Dublin online edition, the transcribed and searchable base on which any victim-level database would be built.

items.title: Reading the 1641 Irish Rebellion
items.note: Examines how news pamphlets reported the rising in England, the channel through which inflated death tolls circulated.

items.title: Women and Sexual Violence in the "1641 Depositions"
items.note: Reads the depositions for evidence of sexual violence against women, attending to the legal framing and silences of the testimony.

items.title: Rereading Rape and Sexual Violence in the Irish Rebellion of 1641
items.note: Reassesses reports of rape in the depositions and how historians have discounted or used them.

items.title: Religion, Rebellion and Violence in Ireland, c. 1603-1649
items.note: First full study of religious violence in early Stuart Ireland, centred on the 1641 rebellion and the depositions.

items.title: The 1641 Depositions and the textual record of historical Irish English
items.note: Treats the depositions as a linguistic corpus, showing that clerical mediation of testimony can be analysed systematically, relevant to coding deponents' voices.
